title: Extension closure of Krause alpha-compact objects
statement: Let $C$ be a locally $v$-small triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] with $v$-small coproducts, and let $\alpha$ be a regular cardinal in universe $v$. If $X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]$ is a distinguished triangle and $X,Z$ are alpha-compact in the support-and-factorization sense [def-sfb-alpha-compact-object], then $Y$ is alpha-compact.

source.place: Krause (2001), Lemma 5, page 124, preservation of G4 under triangles, with the omitted cone argument expanded.

external.place: On Neeman’s Well Generated Triangulated Categories, Documenta Mathematica 6 (2001), pages 124–125.

proof.text: Let S be the canonical maximal class of alpha-compact objects. Its finite extension hull H is the union over n of S.extensionProductIter n. S is replete, contains zero and is shift closed by the alpha-compact API. Associativity of extensionProduct, obtained from the octahedral axiom, makes H extension closed. Thus H is triangulated. Induction on n and the alpha-small extension API show that every H-object is alpha-small.

Prove by induction on the extension length that every map from an H-object to a coproduct factors through a coproduct of H-objects. For a cone U to V to X, factor the restriction from V through V_i in H. Complete V_i to Y_i to fiber triangles F_i to V_i to Y_i. The composite from U into the coproduct of V_i is killed in the coproduct of Y_i. Applying the opposite-product distinguished-triangle theorem gives a lift into the coproduct of F_i. Factor this lift through U_i in H. Form the cones W_i of U_i to V_i, which belong to H. Complete the induced square U to V to a morphism into a cone triangle of the coproduct map. Exactness maps this cone into the coproduct of W_i. The resulting map from X agrees with the given map on V. Their difference therefore factors through U[1]; its inductive factorization is combined componentwise with W_i by a binary biproduct. This gives G4 for H.
Since every H-object is alpha-small and H satisfies G4, H is contained in S by the existential definition of alpha-compactness. Every extension of S-objects lies in H, so it lies in S.

proof_origin.place: Krause (2001), Lemma 5, page 124, preservation of G4 under triangles, with the omitted cone argument expanded.
